correctness.rationale: PASS. For n>=6 the four ±1,±2 neighbors are distinct. Direct gap analysis proves: every cyclic gap between selected vertices is 1..4; each gap of four must be flanked by two gaps of one, and this condition suffices for every outside vertex to have 0 or >=2 fort neighbors. Counting 4-to-1 incidences yields a<=b and n=3m+a-2b-c<=3m, so |F|>=ceil(n/3). Explicit gap words attain this. At minimum size, the deficit delta=3m-n equals 2b+c-a; exhaustive small-deficit patterns give all-three, one-two, one-one, two-two, and the sole alternating 1,4,1,4 n=10 anomaly. Rooted cyclic-gap word double-counting (n/m) yields counts 3, n, n(n+5)/6+5*1_{n=10}. Independent bitmask enumeration on every subset n=6..13 matched the gap biconditional and exact minimum counts; the source verifier/certificate independently extends checks to n=24 but neither proves the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified by an inaccessible closely related circulant paper. The minimum fort size, equivalently graph spark or n minus failed zero forcing number, is a known numerical corollary and expressly not claimed new. The assessed novel object is the complete cyclic-gap structural classification of all forts and number of minimum-cardinality forts, including 5 isolated n=10 anomalies. Earlier 2024 minimal-fort paper treats inclusion-minimal forts of ordinary cycles and other graph families; generic spark/failed-forcing equivalences yield only a number. The 2025 Gomez et al. paper targets circulant failed zero forcing and might have an uninspected optimal-configuration classification; only its abstract could be inspected; authorized institutional full text request gave vpn_disconnected. This is a genuine residual priority risk, not grounds by itself to reject the statement.
